newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAL plans tie-up with Burmese airline.
newsitem.headline: JAL plans tie-up with Burmese airline.

text.p: Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) said on Tuesday it and Myanma Airways International are planning to jointly operate nonstop flights between Japan and Rangoon in the future.
But no specific date has been set because of the Burmese airline's need to strengthen its service and facilities and the country's unstable political and economic situation, a JAL spokesman said.
Myanma Airways International is owned 51 percent by the state-run domestic carrier Myanma Airways, he said.
The JAL spokesman said the two airlines have already started cooperating in connecting JAL flights from different points in Japan with Burmese flights headed to Rangoon, all via Bangkok.
Demand for flights to Burma is on the rise as an increasing number of Japanese food and textile companies invest there, he added.
Rival All Nippon Airways Co Ltd began operating direct flights twice a week from Osaka to Rangoon in July.
